h: Every Journey and Shabbos Raise the Soul Toward Its Rest

p: אֵלֶּה מַסְעֵי בְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל וְגוֹ׳ (בְּמִדְבַּר לג, א-ב)
"These are the journeys of the Children of Israel," etc. (Bamidbar 33:1–2);
for their journeys by the word of Hashem,
and these are their journeys by their goings forth."
in the name of Rabbi Moshe HaDarshan,
and also the reason of the Rambam, of blessed memory,
a matter whose secret has not been revealed to us;
not as Rabbi Avraham ibn Ezra said,
who said that it is joined to 'for their journeys,'
for the Torah has already informed us of that:
'By the word of Hashem they would encamp
וְעַל פִּי ה׳ יִסָּעוּ (בְּמִדְבַּר ט, כ)
and by the word of Hashem they would journey' (Bamidbar 9:20)";
the reason of Rabbi Moshe HaDarshan
and the reason of the Rambam, of blessed memory,
were not sufficient in his eyes.
We must also understand the wording,
their goings forth for their journeys,"
"and these are their journeys by their goings forth,"
of what it wrote just before.
כְּלוֹמַר שֶׁהַכֹּל הָיָה עַל פִּי ה׳
"That is to say, everything was by the word of Hashem,
But this needs to be understood:
after all, afterward, when it says,
"and these are their journeys by their goings forth,"
לֹא כְּתִיב שָׁם עַל פִּי ה׳
"by the word of Hashem" is not written there!
The whole matter also needs explanation:
why was it necessary to write
"their goings forth for their journeys," or the reverse?
from the place from which they went out!
that it is written in the Torah,
"And they journeyed from such-and-such a place
and encamped in such-and-such a place,"
"And they journeyed and encamped in such-and-such a place,"
so why did it specify a second time
the name of the place from which they journeyed?
About this the pasuk informed us
of the place from which they went out for their journeys
was by the word of Hashem,
Who commanded him to write it so:
that they journeyed from such-and-such a place
and encamped in such-and-such a place.
it is written in the sefarim
that they correspond to the Forty-Two-Letter Name
(as is written in the sefer Tzror HaMor);
and Rabbi Shimshon of Ostropoli, of blessed memory,
and they explained that they were in doubt
about places that had the same letter,
such as the gimmel of the Name אב״ג
or of נג״ד, and the like.
is the Name for the ascents of the soul,
or for ascending to the Pardes.
And the matter of the journeys
was according to what is said
"And it was when the Ark journeyed," etc.,
and let those who hate You flee from before You."
The intent of "those who hate You"
for they had none in the wilderness;
rather, the meaning of "those who hate You" is
those who make Hashem Yisbarach hated
and that is the yetzer hara;
and with this the wording "mesanecha" is justified,
in order to be saved from the yetzer hara,
along the lines of what we explained
"And the Ark of the Covenant of Hashem journeyed before them
to be refined from the three kelipos
which stand opposite, one against the other,
to the three attributes of the Avos,
"to seek out a resting place for them,"
that is, to enter Eretz Yisrael immediately,
which is the place of rest.
"And when it rested he would say (Bamidbar 10:36):
מִלְּשׁוֹן בְּשׁוּבָה וָנַחַת תִּוָּשֵׁעוּן (יְשַׁעְיָה ל, טו)
as in "In stillness and rest shall you be saved" (Yeshayahu 30:15),
which is expounded (Yerushalmi, beginning of the first perek of Taanis)
"Return, Hashem, to the myriads of thousands of Yisrael,"
to mean that the Shechinah does not rest
עַל פָּחוֹת מִב׳ אֲלָפִים וּב׳ רְבָבוֹת
on fewer than two thousand and two myriads
that is, a resting of the Shechinah
than the resting of the Shechinah that exists
onto the weekdays that follow it,
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה בָּא הַשַּׁבָּת הַב׳
and through this the second Shabbos comes
All the days of a person are like this:
there is the journeying and going forward
and when Shabbos comes, rest comes,
for then he is in the state of rest;
כִּי הוֹלֵךְ הָאָדָם אֶל בֵּית עוֹלָמוֹ
"For man goes to his eternal home,"
has a dwelling of his own;
וּבַמִּדְרָשׁ (שְׁמוֹת רַבָּה פָּרָשַׁת פְּקוּדֵי נב, ג)
and in the Midrash (Shemos Rabbah, Parshas Pekudei, 52:3):
הֲוָה לֵיהּ עוֹלָם בִּפְנֵי עַצְמוֹ וְכוּלֵּי
"He has a world of his own," etc.,
That is, all the days of a person
in all six weekdays, he is
in the state of one who goes,
and the rest is on Shabbos;
onto the weekdays that follow it,
for "And it was when it journeyed";
and afterward, on the second Shabbos,
all the days of his life
until he is completed in full perfection,
and then he has no further business

p: In the wilderness they journeyed on each journey,
and at the encampment they attained the holiness
of one letter of the Forty-Two-Letter Name;
and afterward there was a new journey,
according to the holiness of the encampment
This is what is said: "And Moshe wrote
אֶת מוֹצָאֵיהֶם לְמַסְעֵיהֶם עַל פִּי ה׳
their goings forth for their journeys by the word of Hashem";
was according to the going forth,
as they went out from the previous encampment,
and this was written by the word of Hashem:
the going forth and the journey,
as in "And they journeyed from Sukkos
"And these are their journeys by their goings forth":
according to the holiness of the going forth,
the place from which they went out,
in all the holiness of the forty-two letters
there would already have been then
that will be in the future,
שֶׁהָיָה נִכְנָס מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
for Moshe Rabbeinu, peace be upon him, would have entered.
it may be that one needs
in order to merit one letter
according to what is in his power to merit,
and has no business in this world.
וְזֶה עִנְיַן מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ (שַׁבָּת קיח, ב)
This is the meaning of what they said (Shabbos 118b):
radiates the holiness onto the weekdays,
and afterward comes the second Shabbos,
which is loftier than the Shabbos that preceded it,
and they merit a Shabbos as it should be kept,
so that he will be redeemed completely.
וְזֶה עִנְיַן מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ בְּמִדְרָשׁ רַבָּה
This is the meaning of what they said in the Midrash Rabbah
and the holy Zohar, and elsewhere)
that through one Shabbos kept as it should be,
This is regarding the community as a whole.
has a world of his own,
in that he is always going during the weekdays,
the aspect of "And it was when it journeyed,"
and on Shabbos is the rest;
and each Shabbos is loftier than the one before,
וְאֵין לוֹ עֵסֶק עוֹד בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה
and has no further business in this world.
and there be fulfilled in him
"May you see your world in your lifetime";
is given a taste of the fruit of his deeds";
whom HaKadosh Baruch Hu gave a taste,
of something like the World to Come,
וּבְתַנָּא דְבֵי אֵלִיָּהוּ (סֵדֶר אֵלִיָּהוּ רַבָּה פֶּרֶק ה)
and in Tanna d'Vei Eliyahu (Seder Eliyahu Rabbah, perek 5),
without suffering and without the yetzer hara
from what HaKadosh Baruch Hu is destined
to give the tzaddikim in the time to come.
